sections.readable_text:
A parabola is given by [MATH: y=f(x),] where
[MATH: f(x) = x^2 + 8x + 5.]
The function [MATH: g] is defined by [MATH: g(x) = f(x - 5).] What is the vertex of [MATH: y = g(x)?]

sections.normalized_html:
We start by noting the following:

  • Since [MATH: g(x) = f(x - 5),] the graph of [MATH: y = g(x)] is obtained by shifting the graph of [MATH: y = f(x)] by [MATH: 5] units to the right.

  • Therefore, to obtain the corresponding points on [MATH: y = g(x),] we add [MATH: 5] to each [MATH: x]-coordinate of [MATH: y = f(x)] while keeping the [MATH: y]-coordinate unchanged.

Now, recall that the [MATH: x]-coordinate of the vertex of a quadratic function [MATH: y = ax^2 + bx + c] is [MATH: x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}.]

Here, [MATH: a = 1] and [MATH: b = 8], so the [MATH: x]-coordinate of the vertex of [MATH: y = f(x)] is [MATH: x|= − (8)/(2(1)); = − 4.]

Next, to find the [MATH: y]-coordinate of the vertex of [MATH: y = f(x),] we substitute [MATH: x = -4] into [MATH: f(x){:}] [MATH: f(x)|= x^{2} + 8x + 5; f(− 4)|= (− 4)^{2} + 8(− 4) + 5; = 16 − 32 + 5; = − 11]

So, the vertex of [MATH: y = f(x)] is [MATH: (-4,-11).]

Therefore, adding [MATH: 5] to the [MATH: x]-coordinate, the vertex of [MATH: y = g(x)] is [MATH: (-4+5, -11) = \left(1, -11\right).]

[MATH: g(x) = (x-7)(x+5).]
Suppose the function [MATH: g] is defined by [MATH: g(x) = f(x-6).] What is the vertex of [MATH: y = f(x)?]

sections.normalized_html:
We start by noting the following:

  • Since [MATH: g(x) = f(x - 6),] the graph of [MATH: y = g(x)] is obtained by shifting the graph of [MATH: y = f(x)] by [MATH: 6] units to the right.

  • Therefore, the graph of [MATH: y = f(x)] is obtained by shifting the graph of [MATH: y = g(x)] by [MATH: 6] units to the left.

  • So, to obtain the corresponding points on [MATH: y = f(x),] we subtract [MATH: 6] from each [MATH: x]-coordinate of [MATH: y = g(x)] while keeping the [MATH: y]-coordinate unchanged.

From the equation [MATH: g(x) = (x-7)(x+5),] we find that the roots of the parabola are [MATH: x_1=7] and [MATH: x_2=-5.]

To find the [MATH: x]-coordinate of the vertex of [MATH: y = g(x),] we take the average of the roots, as follows:

[MATH: x|= (x_{1} + x_{2})/(2); = (7 + (− 5))/(2); = (2)/(2); = 1]

Next, to find the [MATH: y]-coordinate of the vertex of [MATH: y = g(x),] we substitute [MATH: x = 1] into [MATH: g(x){:}]
[MATH: g(x)|= (x − 7)(x + 5); g(1)|= (1 − 7)(1 + 5); = (− 6)(6); = − 36]

So, the vertex of [MATH: y = g(x)] is [MATH: (1,-36).]

Therefore, subtracting [MATH: 6] from the [MATH: x]-coordinate, the vertex of [MATH: y = f(x)] is [MATH: (1-6, -36) = \left(-5, -36\right).]
